newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil coffee crop may reach 22 mln bags - govt.
newsitem.headline: Brazil coffee crop may reach 22 mln bags - govt.

text.p: Brazil's 1997/98 coffee crop could be up to 22 million 60-kg bags, said the head of the primary commodities department at the Industry and Commerce Ministry.
"It's between 20 and 22 million bags," Mauricio Assis told reporters after a meeting with soluble coffee industry representatives.
"We're working with a forecast of around 20 million with a variation of 10 percent," he added.
In January, Assis told an international coffee conference that the government was working with an estimate of between 18 and 20 million bags for the 1997/98 harvest.
Assis was attending a meeting to discuss how to solve problems hitting the soluble coffee industry. Other participants included exporters and roasting industry representatives.
After a discussion of the market situation, Assis said that exports were progressing at a good pace and should reach 1.1 million bags in February and one million bags in March.
Under a scheme agreed with other producing countries, Brazil should not export more than six million bags in January to June.
Looking ahead to 1997/98, Assis said that arabica producing countries would have to discuss whether to maintain export quotas in view of an evident shortage in world supply.
"This is an analysis that has to be completed. It's a decision of the Association of the Coffee Producing Countries. The matter will be discussed in May," Assis said.
